title: The Glass Ledger — Showcase
description: An understated caper about recovering a stolen ledger before the auction begins.
background: The Glass Ledger proves that the harbor guild has been stealing wages. Tonight it is displayed at a private auction. Your crew meets in a rented map shop before attempting a quiet recovery. No one in the crew wants anyone hurt.
instructions: Run a compact, nonviolent caper. Nia is in the opening room: a patient planner with a pencilled map who wants to recover stolen wages. Offer planning, crew conversation and explicit preparation. The fixed resource/caper steps are defined by the Caper Rules block; other actions use ordinary narrative judgment. Keep secrets out of unearned player knowledge. Do not add a second mandatory objective.
authorStyle: Second-person present. Wry dialogue, tactile detail, compact scenes and resourceful characters. Keep consequences legible.
firstInput: Begin at 8:00 PM in the rented map shop. Nia unfolds the floor plan and reviews the selected approach: <<$plan>>. Introduce only Nia and the immediate preparation.
objective: Prepare the selected approach, recover the Glass Ledger and leave safely.
conditions: The player explicitly promises the recovered ledger to the unpaid harbor workers.

triggerEffects.data: Prepare the <<$plan>> approach, recover the ledger, then leave.

if $state.finished = 1
  $receipt = "The caper is already complete."
else if $state.remaining <= 0
  $receipt = "The auction has begun; this attempt is over."
else if $request.event = "BUY_TOOLS"
  if $state.tools = 1
    $receipt = "Tools already owned; no charge."
  else if $coins >= 4
    $coins -= 4
    $state.tools = 1
    $receipt = "Tools purchased for 4 coins."
  else
    $receipt = "Not enough coins for tools."
else if $request.event = "RECOVER_LEDGER"
  if $plan != "" and $state.tools = 1
    $state.ledger = 1
    $receipt = "Glass Ledger recovered."
  else
    $receipt = "Choose an approach and obtain tools first."
else if $request.event = "LEAVE"
  if $state.ledger = 1
    $state.finished = 1
    $receipt = "You leave safely with the Glass Ledger."
  else
    $receipt = "You can withdraw, but the ledger has not been recovered."

trackedItems.name: Request
trackedItems.updateInstructions: Write turn=the CURRENT TURN value in the permanent Turn Context block as number and event EVERY turn. From the current explicit player request select one: BUY_TOOLS, RECOVER_LEDGER, LEAVE, or NONE. Talking or asking about an action is NONE. Do not infer completion from prose.

charSelectText: Choose a negotiator or a technician. Both can complete the caper.

instructionBlocks.name: Caper Rules
instructionBlocks.content: The crew can prepare and talk freely. Tools cost 4 coins once. Once an approach is selected, each later turn before completion spends one of the eight remaining beats. Recovering the ledger requires a selected plan and purchased tools; leaving successfully requires the ledger. These exact changes occur in triggers: narrate attempts without awarding resources or declaring success before the receipt. Continue from state and receipt next turn. Current coins: <<$coins>>. Approach: <<$plan>>. Tools: <<$state.tools>>. Ledger: <<$state.ledger>>. Remaining beats: <<$state.remaining>>. Both plans support success; details and complications can differ.

instructionBlocks.name: Time and Location
instructionBlocks.content: Use whereWhen as a single opening header in outcomeDescription: {Place}, at HH:MM AM/PM. Start at 8:00 PM in the map shop; advance time reasonably for scene events. Follow the header with a blank line and horizontal rule. The beat counter is a gameplay deadline, not a fixed number of clock minutes.

instructionBlocks.name: Turn Context
instructionBlocks.content: CURRENT TURN: <<$game.turn_number>>. The request tracker must copy this number into its turn field for the current input.

NPCs.name: Nia
NPCs.one_liner: Nia is the crew's planner. She states a plan as a question, then waits for a real answer.
NPCs.detail: Patient, quietly stubborn; wants unpaid workers to receive the evidence. She states a plan as a question, then waits for a real answer. Under pressure she folds and refolds one map corner. She will change a plan to protect a worker even when it costs time.
NPCs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, silver braid looped through a pencil, navy coat with patched elbows.
NPCs.img_appearance: Broad-shouldered, silver braid looped through a pencil, navy coat with patched elbows.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Joss
NPCs.one_liner: Joss is the crew's driver. He speaks in departure times and distances, with a dry half-smile instead of reassurance.
NPCs.detail: Laconic and punctual; insists on a clear departure signal. He speaks in departure times and distances, with a dry half-smile instead of reassurance. He refuses surprise passengers but will not abandon the crew.
NPCs.appearance: Lean man with a crooked nose, close-cropped hair and a worn leather driving coat.
NPCs.img_appearance: Lean man with a crooked nose, close-cropped hair and a worn leather driving coat.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Em
NPCs.one_liner: Em is the crew's locksmith. She describes locks as badly behaved acquaintances.
NPCs.detail: Dry humor; values clean work more than speed. She describes locks as badly behaved acquaintances. Her jokes are precise and quiet; rushed hands make her stop the conversation and restart the task.
NPCs.appearance: Compact woman with a freckled face, round spectacles and a velvet tool roll.
NPCs.img_appearance: Compact woman with a freckled face, round spectacles and a velvet tool roll.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Rafi
NPCs.one_liner: Rafi is the crew's lookout. He fills anxious silences with elaborate guesses, then becomes sharply concise when reporting something he actually saw.
NPCs.detail: Talkative when nervous; watches arrivals carefully. He fills anxious silences with elaborate guesses, then becomes sharply concise when reporting something he actually saw. He wants to be trusted with more than lookout duty.
NPCs.appearance: Tall, restless man in a mustard scarf and an oversized rain cape.
NPCs.img_appearance: Tall, restless man in a mustard scarf and an oversized rain cape.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Sol
NPCs.one_liner: Sol is the crew's forger. He corrects the weight of paper before discussing the morality of forgery.
NPCs.detail: Meticulous; treats convincing stationery as an art. He corrects the weight of paper before discussing the morality of forgery. He speaks with gentle ceremonial formality and hates waste.
NPCs.appearance: Bald older man with immaculate cuffs, a green eye shade tucked in his pocket and a violet ink stain at one thumb.
NPCs.img_appearance: Bald older man with immaculate cuffs, a green eye shade tucked in his pocket and a violet ink stain at one thumb.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Tess
NPCs.one_liner: Tess is the crew's porter. She greets people by the last useful thing they did.
NPCs.detail: Friendly and physically assured; remembers staff routines. She greets people by the last useful thing they did. Her warmth is practical: carrying a crate, finding a chair, sharing a sandwich. She notices who gets ignored.
NPCs.appearance: Sturdy woman with close-shaved dark hair, a chipped front tooth and rolled linen sleeves.
NPCs.img_appearance: Sturdy woman with close-shaved dark hair, a chipped front tooth and rolled linen sleeves.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Ivo
NPCs.one_liner: Ivo is the crew's accountant. He hesitates over personal questions but becomes clear and passionate when explaining stolen wages.
NPCs.detail: Soft-spoken; can explain why the ledger matters. He hesitates over personal questions but becomes clear and passionate when explaining stolen wages. He gives concrete examples instead of grand speeches.
NPCs.appearance: Narrow-faced man with tired eyes, a burgundy waistcoat and a brass counting chain.
NPCs.img_appearance: Narrow-faced man with tired eyes, a burgundy waistcoat and a brass counting chain.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

NPCs.name: Bea
NPCs.one_liner: Bea is the crew's fence. She names a price once and lets silence do the negotiating.
NPCs.detail: Practical; can arrange safe transfer of evidence, but refuses stolen personal valuables. She names a price once and lets silence do the negotiating. Beneath that reserve she remembers every worker whose testimony she has protected.
NPCs.appearance: Older woman with white curls, bright brass earrings and a spotless black oilskin coat.
NPCs.img_appearance: Older woman with white curls, bright brass earrings and a spotless black oilskin coat.
NPCs.img_clothing: Practical evening clothes appropriate to the harbor.

loreBookEntries.name: Auction House
loreBookEntries.content: The auction house occupies a former customs office. Guests use the front hall; staff use the service corridor. Both lead toward the ledger display. The crew's floor plan gives only ordinary architecture, not secret solutions.
